title: JARID2 Inhibition Reprograms Human Hematopoietic Progenitor Cells To Enhance Bone Marrow Transplantation
description: Hematopoietic stem cell transplantation is a common treatment for many blood disorders. Umbilical cord blood (UCB) serves as a valuable source of hematopoietic stem and progenitor cells (HSPCs), particularly for patients lacking a matched donor. However, the limited number of repopulating cells in UCB units restricts its clinical utility. Here, we demonstrate that JARID2 knockdown, distinct from EZH2 loss, increases both the number and functionality of human UCB-derived HSPCs in vitro and in vivo. After ex vivo culture, these functionally enhanced HSPCs were identified as CD34⁺CD90⁺EPCR⁺CD49f⁻CD71⁻. Mechanistically, JARID2 knockdown promotes a quiescent, long-term self-renewal gene expression program by upregulating STAT1 and MHC class II. Notably, it also confers HSC-like potential to multipotent progenitors (MPPs), enhancing their regenerative capacity. These findings support JARID2 inhibition as a safe and reversible strategy to expand functional HSPCs from UCB ex vivo, potentially increasing access to this life-saving therapy for a broader patient population. Overall design: To investigate the molecular mechanisms underlying JARID2-KD-mediated expansion and functional enhancement of human HSPCs, enriched umbilical cord blood-derived CD34⁺ cells were transduced with shRenilla, shJARID2, or shEZH2 and cultured ex vivo for 8 days. hCD34⁺ cells were then sorted for CITE-seq analysis. Guided by the CITE-seq findings and complementary functional assays, CD34⁺CD90⁺EPCR⁺CD49f⁻CD71⁻GFP⁺ cells were further isolated after 8 days of ex vivo culture for bulk RNA-seq, CUT&Tag, and CUT&RUN analyses. For scRNA-seq analysis, shRenilla- or shJARID2-transduced CD34⁺ cells were transplanted into NSG mice, and hCD34⁺ cells were recovered from the bone marrow 20 weeks post-transplantation. For STAT1 CUT&RUN, hCD34⁺ cells were collected either directly from cord blood as naïve controls or after 8 days of ex vivo culture following transduction with shRenilla or shJARID2.
